# The generated file

`airtable-schema.ts` is regenerated by the observer on every schema change and written by the daemon. See [`examples/airtable-schema.ts`](../examples/airtable-schema.ts) for a complete one.

## Contents

- **Shared interfaces**: `Attachment`, `Thumbnail`, `Collaborator`, `LinkedRecord`, `SelectChoice`, `LookupValue<T>`, `AiText`.
- **One `*Choice` alias per select field**, e.g. `ProjectsStatusChoice`, a literal union of `{id; name; color?: string}`. Aliases are deduped across tables.
- **One `<Table>Record` interface per table**, every field optional (empty cells are absent). Values mirror what `record.getCellValue(field)` returns in the Blocks SDK, not the flatter REST shapes:
  - selects: the choice union; links: `LinkedRecord[]`; collaborators: `Collaborator`; attachments: `Attachment[]` with thumbnails
  - formulas and rollups resolve to their result type; lookups to `Array<LookupValue<Result>>`, each entry `{linkedRecordId, value}`
  - `aiText` is `AiText`, `externalSyncSource` is `SelectChoice`, barcode `{text; type?}`, button `{label; url}`
  - a field type airgen doesn't know is `unknown`, with the type named in the JSDoc
- **One `<Table>Write` interface per table**: only writable fields, each in the SDK's documented cell write format. Scalars admit `null` (clear), dates take `string | Date`, selects `{id} | {name}` indexed off the read alias, collaborators `{id}`, links `{id; name?}` (the interface flavor also accepts a bare `{name}` to create and link), attachments `{url; filename?}` or an existing `Attachment`. Computed fields are omitted rather than `never`, so the interface doubles as the partial update payload. Barcode has no write format in the SDK and is omitted.
- **`airgenMeta`** as const: `version` (2), `baseId`, `signature`, and per table `id`, `name`, `primaryFieldId`, and a field map with `id`, raw `name`, `type`, `isComputed`, select `choices` (display order, with `color`), and the computed `result` type.
- **`TableRecordMap`, `TableKey`, `TableWriteMap`** for inference.
- **`export const {useRecords, useTable, useSchemaDrift, useFields, useMutations, useQuery} = createTypedHooks<TableRecordMap, TableWriteMap>(airgenMeta)`**, which is what makes the hooks usable from plain JS.

## Names

All names are transliterated first (Latin accents stripped: `soluções` becomes `solucoes`). Table names become PascalCase (`My Table`; a collision gets a numeric suffix, `MyTable2`; a digit-leading name a `T` prefix, `T2024Plans`). Field keys are camelCased (`Contact Email` becomes `contactEmail`; all-caps words fold, `ID` becomes `id`), deduped per table (`Soluções` and `Solucoes` become `solucoes` and `solucoes2`), prefixed with `_` when digit-leading, and fall back to the quoted raw name when nothing survives (an emoji-only name). The raw Airtable name is always kept in the meta and the field's JSDoc.

## Rename survival

Types are erased at compile time, so no tool can update types at runtime. What airgen does instead:

- Every hook resolves tables and fields **by ID** from `airgenMeta`, so renaming a table, field, or select choice in Airtable never breaks the running extension.
- The observer sees the same schema event and regenerates the file, so the display names in your types refresh while you develop.
- A deleted or hidden field is skipped; a deleted or hidden table reads as `[]`, and writes to it fail with a `table-missing` issue instead of throwing.

## Efficiency

Three gates keep generation cheap:

1. `useWatchable(base, ['schema'])`: the observer re-renders only on schema mutations, never on record or cell changes. Keep it a leaf component.
2. A canonical schema signature (FNV-1a) is compared before anything else, so no-op events skip generation.
3. Generation runs inside a 500 ms debounce, so a burst of edits costs one generation and one POST. The daemon also skips the disk write when the content is unchanged.
